title: Binary search, five ways
description:
Write these with your own binary searches (the standard `lower_bound` family is off limits here):

```cpp
std::size_t lowerBound(const std::vector<int>& a, int x);    // first index with a[i] >= x (a.size() if none)
std::size_t upperBound(const std::vector<int>& a, int x);    // first index with a[i] > x
int searchRotated(const std::vector<int>& a, int x);         // index of x in a rotated sorted vector of distinct values, or -1
long long minSpeed(const std::vector<int>& piles, long long hours);   // binary search on the answer
unsigned long long sqrtFloor(unsigned long long n);          // the largest r with r * r <= n
```

- `searchRotated`: `a` was sorted ascending, then rotated, like `{ 15, 18, 22, 3, 5, 9, 12 }`. O(log n).
- `minSpeed`: a worker eats from piles of bananas; each hour they pick one pile and eat up to `speed` bananas from it (finishing a smaller pile still uses the whole hour). Return the smallest whole `speed` that finishes all piles within `hours` hours. `hours` is at least the number of piles. A pile of `p` takes `ceil(p / speed)` hours.
- `sqrtFloor` must be exact for every 64-bit `n`, without floating point. Beware of `mid * mid` overflowing: compare `mid <= n / mid` instead.
hints: When the answer is the **largest** value that works, round `mid` up (`lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2`) and set `lo = mid` on success; otherwise a two-element range never shrinks.
In `searchRotated`, compare `a[lo]` with `a[mid]`: if `a[lo] <= a[mid]`, the left half is in order, and you can tell at once whether `x` lies in it.
rules: Find the square root with a binary search on whole numbers.
